references.title: Jean-Jacques Rousseau, Discourse on the Origin and Foundations of Inequality, Part II, Ian Johnston translation
references.support: Rousseau's Part II deer-and-hare passage was read directly in Ian Johnston's English translation. It supports the historical narrative attribution, not a formal payoff matrix or equilibrium analysis.

references.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Prisoner’s Dilemma
references.support: Relevant sections 1 and 8 were read: they explain the Prisoner's Dilemma conditions and contrast them with the stag hunt, including its typical payoffs, equilibria and risk-dominance condition. The entry presents its numerical matrix as typical, not unique.

references.title: Brian Skyrms, “The Stag Hunt”
references.support: Relevant passages of the scholarly paper were read, including the model and trust discussion (pp. 1–4) and population/evolutionary extensions (pp. 10–15). The analysis shows that such outcomes depend on specified dynamics and interaction structure.
